evals.prompt: Review this for our MoonPay Enterprise landing page: 'MoonPay, the leading crypto payments company, now processes $170 billion a year through Paysafe. With zero fees and instant settlement, MoonPay Enterprise is the only platform fintechs need. We recently acquired North Capital to bring tokenized securities to every customer.'
evals.expected_output: A review table flagging each planted violation with severity, rule, and on-canon fix, then a Blocked verdict and the canon stamp.
assertions: Opens with the review table, not a restatement of the draft
Flags 'the leading crypto payments company' as Block under B1
Flags the $170 billion as Paysafe volume misattributed to MoonPay (B9)
Flags 'zero fees' as Block (B4 or C8)
Flags 'instant settlement' (B10)
Flags 'the only platform' (B2)
Flags 'acquired North Capital' as Block and gives the C5 wording with 'subject to regulatory approval'
Gives a verdict of Blocked
Ends with 'Canon v2026-09-28'

evals.prompt: Write a 3-sentence LinkedIn post announcing MoonPay Enterprise for payroll and HR platform leaders.
evals.expected_output: An on-canon post leading with P2 for the enterprise overlay, using only approved numbers with scope, followed by a claim sources table and the canon stamp.
assertions: Leads with the one-integration message (P2), not a table-stakes claim
Any Deel figure says 'more than 40,000 businesses across the UK and EU' and is not framed as MoonPay customers
Uses 'MoonPay Enterprise' and never 'MoonPay for Business'
Uses no competitor names
Includes a claim sources table after the copy
Ends with 'Canon v2026-09-28'

evals.prompt: How many enterprise customers does MoonPay have? Sales wants one number for a deck.
evals.expected_output: Answer mode: explains the two scoped figures (500+ company-wide vs 50+ MoonPay Enterprise partners), says which to use when, and warns against mixing them.
assertions: Leads with approved wording from the Approved numbers table
Distinguishes 'more than 500 enterprise customers' (company-wide) from 'more than 50 enterprise partners' (MoonPay Enterprise)
Warns not to combine or swap the two scopes
Stays under about 80 words
Ends with 'Canon v2026-09-28'

evals.prompt: How should we position MoonPay against Circle's payments network in a customer email?
evals.expected_output: Escalation: Circle is not in the internal competitor list, and customer-facing copy never names competitors. Offers the 'old way' frame as the on-canon alternative.
assertions: States that the competitor is not in canon and to check with PMM
States that customer-facing copy does not name competitors
Offers an on-canon alternative framed against stitching multiple providers
Does not invent positioning claims about Circle

evals.prompt: Review this press release sentence: 'MoonPay holds a New York BitLicense, a New York Limited Purpose Trust Charter, and money transmitter licenses across the United States, and has MiCA authorization in the EU to provide on- and off-ramps. MoonPay is how the world moves value.'
evals.expected_output: A one-line confirmation that the sentence is on-canon, with no invented flags, and the canon stamp.
assertions: Says the draft has no issues or is Ready
Does not invent Fix or Block flags
Ends with 'Canon v2026-09-28'

evals.prompt: Draft a hero line for MoonPay's AI agent page. Say the MoonAgents Card works everywhere Mastercard is accepted worldwide.
evals.expected_output: Draft mode that refuses to drop the C4 availability qualifier, writes an on-canon hero with the qualifier in the subhead, and explains the change in one line.
assertions: Does not claim worldwide availability
Includes the C4 qualifier: live in the UK and Latin America, with US and EU expansion planned
Leads with P4 for the agent audience
Explains the deviation from the brief in one line
Ends with 'Canon v2026-09-28'
